requirements: Implement a minimal QEMU SysBus model for STM32F103 TIM2 at base 0x40000000.
Use virtual time (QEMU timer) rather than host threads or wall clock.
Support 16-bit upcounter, update events, and four output-compare channels.
Implement registers: CR1, CR2, SMCR, DIER, SR, EGR, CCMR1, CCMR2, CCER, CNT, PSC, ARR, CCR1-4, DCR, DMAR.
Implement reset values as specified in reference.md.
Implement counting behavior: starts with CEN, pauses when CEN cleared, tick period = (PSC_active + 1) / 72 MHz.
Implement overflow after ARR_active + 1 ticks, reset CNT to zero, set UIF unless updates disabled.
Implement PSC buffering: UG or overflow transfers PSC preload to active divider.
Implement ARR buffering: immediate when ARPE=0, transferred on update when ARPE=1.
Implement UG behavior: resets CNT, transfers preloads, sets UIF unless URS or UDIS.
Implement UDIS suppression of update-event effects including preload transfer.
Implement URS: prevents software UG from setting UIF but does not block preload transfer.
Implement OPM: clears CEN after next update.
Implement output-compare match: sets CCxIF on match, repeats each period, CCR > active ARR never matches.
Implement CCxG writes: set corresponding CCxIF flag.
Implement interrupt output: level-sensitive, asserted when any enabled flag is set, cleared immediately when no enabled flag remains.

Implement rc_w0 semantics for SR: writing 0 clears bits that were observed (i.e., write 1 to clear? Actually reference says rc_w0: clear only flags observed; driver writes ~pending, so writing 0 to bits clears them).
Implement little-endian MMIO for 32-bit aligned accesses; unsupported accesses should log guest errors.
Ensure deterministic reset state, interrupt level, pending virtual timer, and register/preload state.
Provide qtest suite proving timing boundaries and interrupt clearing.
Provide machine-readable manifest and report.
Follow QEMU conventions and keep implementation small.

register_model.name: SR
register_model.note: Writing 0 to a flag clears it; writing 1 leaves it unchanged.

behavior_model: Maintain internal state: active PSC, active ARR, current CNT, pending timer, interrupt level.
Use QEMU timer to schedule next event (overflow or compare match) based on current active PSC and ARR.
When CEN is set, start counting from current CNT; schedule next event at earliest of overflow and compare matches.
When CEN is cleared, stop timer and cancel pending timer; preserve CNT and active state.
On timer expiry, advance CNT to the event count, set appropriate flags (UIF or CCxIF), then schedule next event.
Overflow: when CNT reaches ARR_active, set CNT to 0, set UIF (unless UDIS), transfer PSC and ARR preloads (unless UDIS), and if OPM set, clear CEN.
Compare match: when CNT equals CCRx and channel is output-configured (CCxS==0), set CCxIF.
UG write: reset CNT to 0, transfer PSC and ARR preloads (unless UDIS), set UIF unless URS or UDIS, and reschedule timer.
CCxG write: set corresponding CCxIF flag.
SR write: for each bit written 0, clear that flag; bits written 1 are unchanged.
Interrupt output: assert if (SR & DIER & 0x1F) != 0; deassert otherwise.
When DIER or SR changes, update interrupt output.
When PSC is written, store preload; active PSC updates on UG or overflow (unless UDIS).
When ARR is written, if ARPE=0, update active ARR immediately and reschedule; if ARPE=1, store preload and update on update event.
When CNT is written, update current count and reschedule.
When CCRx is written, update compare value and reschedule.
Reset: clear all registers to reset values, cancel timer, deassert IRQ.
Unsupported accesses (e.g., non-32-bit, out-of-window) should log guest error and be safe.
All timing calculations use virtual time; round up next deadline so interrupt is not observed before hardware tick.
tests: Reset test: after reset, all registers have reset values, IRQ deasserted, no pending timer.
Basic counting test: set PSC=71, ARR=999, CEN=1; after 1000 ticks (at 72MHz, 1000/1MHz = 1ms), CNT should be 0 and UIF set.
Timing boundary test: at 999 ticks, CNT should be 999 and UIF not set; at 1000 ticks, overflow occurs.
Prescaler test: with PSC=71, tick period is 1us; verify CNT increments at correct virtual time.
Compare match test: set CCR2=250, ARR=999; at 250 ticks, CC2IF set; at 999 ticks, UIF set.
Interrupt clearing test: set DIER with UIE and CC2IE, trigger both flags, assert IRQ; write SR=0 (clear all), assert IRQ deasserted.
UG test: write UG, verify CNT resets to 0, UIF set (unless URS), and PSC/ARR preloads transferred.
UDIS test: set UDIS, trigger overflow, verify UIF not set and preloads not transferred.
URS test: set URS, write UG, verify UIF not set but preloads transferred.
OPM test: set OPM, trigger overflow, verify CEN cleared.
ARPE test: with ARPE=0, write ARR, verify active ARR changes immediately; with ARPE=1, write ARR, verify active ARR changes only on update.
CCxG test: write CC2G, verify CC2IF set.
CCR > ARR test: set CCR2 > ARR, run timer, verify no CC2IF set.
CEN pause test: start timer, clear CEN, advance time, verify CNT unchanged and no flags set.
MMIO access test: read/write all registers, verify values; attempt unsupported access and verify guest error logged.
IRQ level test: assert IRQ when enabled flag set, deassert when cleared.
assumptions: The timer input clock is fixed at 72 MHz; no RCC clock tree modeling.
Registers are 16-bit in effect but accessed via 32-bit MMIO; we will store 16-bit values and mask writes to 16 bits.
Only output-compare mode is modeled; input capture and PWM output are out of scope.
CCxS bits are assumed to be zero (output mode) for compare match behavior; if non-zero, channel is not modeled for capture.
The driver's SR write pattern (write ~pending) implies rc_w0 semantics: writing 0 clears flags, writing 1 leaves unchanged.
The interrupt output is a single line connected to NVIC IRQ 28; we model it as a GPIO out.
The device is memory-mapped at 0x40000000 with a 0x400 byte window.
Unsupported registers (CR2, SMCR, CCER, DCR, DMAR) are stored but have no functional effect.
The timer should use QEMU virtual time and a single QEMU timer for scheduling.
The next deadline should be rounded up to avoid early interrupts.
The model should be deterministic across migration; we will store necessary state in VMState.
risks: Timing precision: rounding up deadlines may cause slight delays but ensures no early interrupts.
Interrupt clearing semantics: rc_w0 might be misinterpreted; driver writes ~pending, so writing 0 clears observed flags; we must implement that.
Preload transfer timing: PSC and ARR buffering must be carefully implemented to match hardware.
Compare match scheduling: multiple compare channels and overflow need to be scheduled correctly; earliest event should trigger.
Counter wrap and CNT writes: writing CNT while timer running must reschedule correctly.
Migration: must save/restore timer state and active preloads to avoid stale host time.
Unsupported accesses: logging guest errors may require QEMU guest_error APIs; ensure safe handling.
qtest timing: virtual time advancement must be precise; tests must account for rounding.
Scope limitations: input capture and PWM are not modeled; tests should not rely on them.
